answer: Each identity must help raise one shared timber barn per epoch: a small verifiable job, a benchmark run or a labelled dataset, added to a public meadow of work. Unrelated peers randomly re-execute a sample; if a contribution fails to reproduce, the identity and anyone who co-signed it lose stake. A willow bends but a fake cannot borrow another's labour: every clone must do its own real work each epoch, and the re-execution lottery means a farm cannot predict which fakes get checked, so mass forgery pays full compute per identity forever.
